extracted.intended_audience: administrators and managers in South African organs of state (public sector decision-makers, legal services, project teams)
extracted.subtask_short: PAJA mainstreaming for organs of state
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for embedding the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act (PAJA) into administrative decision‑making processes in South African organs of state; includes phased implementation, templates, self‑assessment and MPAT alignment. Targeted at administrators, legal personnel and implementation teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions must obey the law and be authorised by law (i.e., be allowed by law and taken by an authorised administrator acting within the scope of the authorisation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each decision is based on an Empowering Provision (law, common law rule, customary law, agreement or instrument). Business processes, forms and letters must record the empowering provision and evidence delegation where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions must be justifiable — there must be a good reason for the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should be based on applicable facts and law; the decision‑maker should be able to explain and justify the reasoning. Record factual and legal bases in the decision record and reasons provided to affected persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedurally fair processes (fair procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrators should follow procedures that enable consultation, representation and communication of a decision and rights; the PAJA sets out procedures to follow before and after decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural fairness includes giving notice of proposed decisions, allowing affected persons to make representations, ensuring impartiality, and following prescribed steps both before and after decisions. Business processes must embed these steps and provide accessible opportunities for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to written reasons / provision of reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected persons have the right to written reasons for administrative actions; it is good practice to give reasons at the time the decision is communicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reasons are provided, they should be clear and in simple language the person can understand. If reasons are not provided, include a notice of the right to request reasons and the procedure for requesting them. Use template wording provided in Information Sheet 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision‑making processes must give notice of the proposed decision, stating clearly what decision is planned and the reason for this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices should explain the proposed action, the legal basis and provide a reasonable opportunity and instructions for making representations. Templates/examples are provided for standard wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to make representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected persons must be given a reasonable opportunity to make a presentation or submit information regarding the proposed decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify reasonable timelines and methods for submissions; provide assistance if a person cannot write; record receipt of representations and how they were considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear communication of the taken decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After a decision is made the administrator must clearly communicate the decision to affected persons and provide reasons and information on rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should state the decision, reasons (if provided), how to request reasons if not provided, internal appeal routes (name, address, timelines), and remedies including judicial review. Use standardised letter templates and record proof of service (receipt, fax report, registered post slip).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and user-friendly processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative decision‑making processes should be accessible, understandable and user‑friendly to citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design processes, notices and reasons in plain language; allow multiple submission channels (email, fax, registered mail, hand delivery); provide office assistance for persons who cannot write; ensure information is available in relevant languages where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing affected persons of review/appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected persons must be informed of their rights to request reasons, to internal appeal and to challenge administrative decisions in court (judicial review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear notices of internal appeal procedures (who to appeal to, address, required content, deadlines) and the right to apply to the High Court for review (including statutory time limits such as 180 days where relevant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision‑maker authority and delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative decisions must be made by those with delegated authority; delegation must be evident and consistent with the empowering provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business processes and records must show who has the authority to make the decision and any delegation of powers. Ensure delegated powers are within the scope permitted by empowering legislation and recorded in process documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions must be based on an Empowering Provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Each decision must be grounded in an empowering provision: a law, rule of common law, customary law, agreement or other instrument authorising the administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and cite the specific empowering provision in notices, decision records and templates. Check that the chosen provision actually authorises the proposed action (e.g., National Road Traffic Act for licence revocation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of plain/simple language in reasons and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons and communications should be written in simple language that the person can understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid legal jargon in templates and letters; provide examples of wording in Information Sheet 5; customise templates to institutional needs while keeping language accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping decision‑making steps (process analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Map out all steps (activities) before, during and after a decision to understand how PAJA requirements interact with business processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of Phase 3, document each activity, identify where notice, representation, decision, communication and remedies occur, and examine handoffs, forms and letters for PAJA compliance. Use the provided database/examples to compare best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify gaps and recommend amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify gaps in existing processes relative to PAJA requirements and make concrete recommendations to address them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gap analysis should flag missing notice steps, unclear empowering provisions, absent delegation records, inadequate templates, or inaccessible communication channels. Recommendations should be translated into amended processes, forms and letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend decision‑making processes, tools and templates (Phase 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate recommendations into amended business processes, standardised letters, forms and tools to ensure PAJA compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work teams should adapt templates from the database (Information Sheet 5), involve legal services in drafting, and ensure amended processes and documents are available for implementation. Self‑assessment indicators for Phase 4 include: review of database examples, legal support involvement, and availability of amended documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self‑assessment progress indicators (Phase 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before moving to implementation, use a self‑assessment tool to check key progress indicators for Phase 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress indicators include: (1) work teams have reviewed the database of examples; (2) legal services personnel have supported tool development; (3) amended decision‑making processes, letters and forms are available. Use the provided self‑assessment checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation planning and capacity building (Phase 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement the amended processes, build staff capacity, and monitor implementation for continuous improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop an implementation plan (Implementation Tool 6), host mini‑training sessions on amended processes/forms/letters, run regular feedback meetings with stakeholders, and use monitoring to find ways to improve practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and continuous improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor the PAJA mainstreaming implementation and continually find ways to improve processes and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish monitoring activities and feedback loops (performance meetings, MPAT reporting), review implementation results, and update processes and training in response to findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment, institutional arrangements and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: PAJA mainstreaming should be aligned with compliance and accountability mechanisms, enabling policy/legislative frameworks, capacity building strategies and relevant government programmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mainstreaming is part of broader PAJA implementation elements — ensure integration with institutional governance, alignment to transversal programmes, and establishment of accountability mechanisms and institutional arrangements to coordinate mainstreaming.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPAT‑aligned performance indicators (PAJA as performance area)
rubrics_metrics.description: Management Performance Assessment Tool (MPAT) includes PAJA implementation in Governance & Accountability and sets standards against which departments are assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant MPAT indicators include: department follows prescribed PAJA procedures; decisions are made under empowering legislation; decisions made by authorised persons; decisions are procedurally fair; prescribed procedures for communicating decisions are followed; department periodically reviews and improves processes; ongoing awareness and capacity building on PAJA. Use MPAT results to assess PAJA implementation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and template requirements (letters and notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications to affected persons (e.g., notice of proposed decision, rejection letters, notices of rights) should include specific information and follow template guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates should include reference/contact details, the decision or proposed decision, reasons (if provided), notice of right to request reasons (if not provided), internal appeal process (who, where, timeline), how to submit representations (email, fax, registered mail, hand), assistance provisions, and retention of proof of service. Examples and sample wording are provided (Information Sheets 5 and 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of proof of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain evidence that communications were received by affected persons (e.g., signed receipt, facsimile transmission report, registered post slip).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include 'Received' acknowledgement sections on letters or retain postal/fax receipts. This supports proof of service for internal processes and potential judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for judicial review and procedural remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform affected persons of statutory time limits and procedural requirements for external remedies (e.g., judicial review time limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, letters should state the time limit for bringing a review (e.g., High Court review within 180 days of receipt of notice under PAJA), and detail procedural steps and points of contact.
